FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by Textile Speciality 
Chemicals and Dyestuffs Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 


The revival of natural dyes has been for two reasons: 
a) Due to the harmful effect of synthetic dyes, globally safer natural dyes are being preferred, and 


b) Ban of azo dyes has also brought back natural dyes in limelight. Natural dyes are being used extensively 
for dyeing of cotton, silk and wool substrate. 


Thus, Catechu dye (Katha) has its own characteristics of being a natural dyestuff and its method of use in 
dyeing and printing these textile substrates. In order to achieve optimum quality with minimum lot to lot variation, 
and variations in dyeing due to same dye of different manufacturers, it is essential to standardize this natural 
dyestuff. This will also lead to minimize cost benefit ratio and help the user to adjust his dyeing or printing recipes 
suitably. 


It is for the first time that the standard for natural dyestuff Catechu dye (Katha) has been formulated. It is mainly 
for the ease of buyers, seller and users of this natural dyestuff. Standardization and identification method will 
bring all the major parameters under scan and match. The main intention of this specification is to identify 
the natural dyestuff from the synthetic analogue which is usually used as adulterant for cost modification and 
colour enhancement purposes. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex F. 


In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or 
calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical 
values (revised). 


IS 17211 : 2019 


Indian Standard 


TEXTILE DYESTUFFS — CATECHU — 
IDENTIFICATION 


1SCOPE 


This standard prescribes test method and identification 
of dried/ aqueous extract of Catechu dye and Catechu 
dyed textiles. The detection and identification of 
synthetic Catechu dye and natural colorant Catechu 
dye are conducted using kit method given in Annex A. 
Confirmatory tests can be carried out through thin 
layer chromatography (TLC) and high performance 
liquid chromatography (HPLC) by chromatographic 
techniques as given in Annex B and C as well as 
by UV-Visible spectroscopic technique as given in 
Annex D. The method for extraction of natural Catechu 
dye from dyed swatches is given in Annex E. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standard contains provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below. 


IS No. 
1070 : 1992 


Title 


Reagent grade water 


3 TERMS AND DEFINITIONS 


For the purposes of this standard, the following terms 
and definitions apply: 


3.1 Catechu — The botanical name of catechu is 
Acacia catechu. It belongs to family Mimosaceae. 
Catechu 1s an extract of Acacia trees used variously 
as a food additive, astringent, tannin, and dye. It is 
extracted from several species of Acacia, but especially 
Senegalia catechu, by boiling the wood in water and 
evaporating the resulting brew. 


3.2 Natural Colour — Colourants from natural origin, 
particularly materials obtained from plant stem, root 
and leaves, extracted without any chemical reaction 
primarily used in textiles for dyeing or printing. 


4 PRINCIPLE 


Natural colourants are usually never a single 
compound. They are composed of several compounds 
which are structurally similar, each of them having 
their characteristic bonding with the fabric based on 
their structure uniqueness. Their contribution in the 
total colourant may vary. Therefore, the analysis of 
these individual components can be carried out by 
chromatographic and spectroscopic techniques. The 
authenticity of the natural colourant can be established 
by these techniques very clearly. 


5PROCEDURE 


5.1 Preparation of Natural Catechu Dye Sample 


Stock solution of natural catechu dye sample is 
prepared in methanol containing 1 000 mg/l catechu. 
This solution is further used after dilution, if necessary, 
for chromatographic and spectroscopic analyses. 


5.2 Analysis 


The detection and identification of natural catechu 
and synthetic brown dye samples are conducted 
using kit method given in Annex A, TLC and HPLC 
by chromatographic techniques as given in Annex B 
and C as well as by UV-Visible as given in Annex D. 
The method for extraction of natural dye from dyed 
swatches is given in Annex E. 


5.3 Qualification and Identification of Natural 
Catechu 


Comparison between analyses of natural catechu and 
synthetic brown dye through 5.3 could show the results 
of discrete differences in synthetic and natural catechu 
sample. The specific tests to be conducted are given 
in Table 1. 


6 REPORT 


The report shall include the following information: 
a) Name of the natural dye tested; 
b) Test method used; and 
c) Identification of the natural source.

ANNEX A 
( Clauses 1, 5.2 and 5.3 ) 


KIT TEST FOR IDENTIFICATION OF NATURAL CATECHU DYE 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


Each natural dye has its characteristic molecular 
composition which is the distinctive feature of that 
dyestuff. Dissolution of the two samples of catechu 
and synthetic brown dye under the class of Kattha 
dyes in different polarity solvents would bring out 
the difference and distinction when compared with 
synthetic brown dye. The catechu dye (Kattha) bearing 
different contaminants dissolves in water layer better, 
whereas the synthetic brown dye dissolves well in 
dichloromethane solvent. 


A-2 APPARATUS 


A-2.1 Test Tubes 

A-2.2 Test Tube Holder 
A-2.3 Electronic Balance 
A-2.4 Spatula 

A-2.5 pH Meter 

A-2.6 Pipette 


A-2.7 Measuring Cylinder 

A-3 REAGENTS 

A-3.1 Water 

A-3.2 Sodium Hydroxide 

A-3.3 Natural Catechu Dye (Kattha) 

A-3.4 Synthetic Brown Dye 

All reagents should be of analytical grade (AR). 


A-4 PROCEDURE 


Catechu dye and brown dye samples (2-5 mg) are 
dissolved in water (10 ml) and made the pH (10.6) 
alkaline by using 10 percent solution of sodium 
hydroxide (NaOH). Dark maroon colour develops in 
the solution having natural catechu while the synthetic 
brown dye remains unchanged in colour. 


A-5 CONCLUSION 


The clear difference in colour identifies the natural 
catechu dye (Kattha) and synthetic brown dye very 
distinctively. 


ANNEX B 
( Clauses 1, 5.2 and 5.3) 


CHROMATOGRAPHIC ANALYSIS — THIN LAYER CHROMATOGRAPHY 


B-1 PRINCIPLE 


Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC) is also used to 
support the identity of a compound in a mixture when 
the R, of a compound is compared with the R, of a 
known compound (preferably both run on the same 
TLC plate). Natural catechu dyes and synthetic brown 
dyes are compared on TLC. 


B-2 APPARATUS 

B-2.1 Silica Coated TLC Plates 
B-2.2 TLC Capillary 

B-2.3 TLC Elution Chamber 
B-2.4 TLC Iodine Chamber 


B-2.5 Electronic Balance — Resolution at 0.001 g. 


B-2.6 Spatula 
B-2.7 Sonicator — To be set at (45 + 2)°C. 


B-2.8 Measuring Cylinder 
B-3 REAGENTS 


B-3.1 Natural Catechu Dye 

B-3.2 Synthetic Reactive Brown Dye 
B-3.3 Ethyl Acetate 

B-3.4 Hexane 

B-3.5 Dichloromethane 


B-3.6 Silica Gel (TLC Grade) 
All reagents should be of analytical grade (AR). 


IS 17211 : 2019 


B-4 PROCEDURE 


Catechu dye sample is prepared by dissolving 0.01 g 
of Kattha sample in 20 ml of solvent such as, ethyl 
acetate or dichloromethane. Reactive brown dye is 
dissolved in similar manner. The prepared sample is 
agitated in sonicator a mechanical agitating device 
used for dissolution of Kattha dye molecules) for 5 min 
for complete dissolution of the catechu samples. The 
solution is then spotted on silica gel coated plate for 
elution. TLC Plates were eluted using 60 percent ethyl 
acetate (EtOAc) /40 percent hexane as suitable eluent 
system for brown dyes. The spots were visualized in 
visible light as well as in iodine chamber. The possible 
constituents of the extracts are identified by comparing 
TLC data, that is, color of the spot and R, values of 
natural catechu and synthetic brown dye.

ANNEX C 
( Clauses 1, 5.2 and 5.3 ) 


IDENTIFICATION OF NATURAL CATECHU DYE BY 
HIGH PERFORMANCE LIQUID CHROMATOGRAPHY (HPLC) METHOD 


C-1 PRINCIPLE 


Identification of compounds by HPLC is a crucial part 
of any HPLC assay. In order to identify any compound 
by HPLC, a detector must first be selected. UV 
detector may be selected and set to optimal detection 
setting and develop a separation assay. The parameters 
of this assay shall be made to be such that a clean 
peak of the both the samples are observed from the 
chromatograph. 


C-2 APPARATUS 

C-2.1 HPLC Machine 

C-2.2 PDA Detector 

C-2.3 C-18 Reverse Phase Column (RPC-C18) 


C-2.4 Electronic Balance — Resolution at 0.001g 
C-2.5 Binary Pump System 

C-2.6 Measuring Cylinder 

C-2.7 Spatula 

C-2.8 Micro Syringe 

C-3 REAGENTS 

C-3.1 Methanol 

C-3.2 De-ionized Water 


C-3.3 Natural Catechu Dye 
NOTE — All solvents used should be HPLC grade only. 


CA PROCEDURE 


The catechu dye sample is prepared by dissolving 0.1 g 
in 1000 ml of methanol and 10 ul of the prepared 
solution is injected to the C-18 reverse phase column 
and eluted through column. The base line shows 
response within a run of 15 min for natural catechu as 
shown in Fig. 2. The parameters of this assay are made 
to be such that a clean peak of the both the samples are 
observed from the chromatograph. 


The experimental conditions are the following: 

a) Eluent: Methanol: Deionised water (80 : 20); 

b) Stationary phase: Column C18, 150 x 4.6 mm; 
5 micron; 

c) Flow Rate: 1.0 ml/min; 

d) Detection Wavelengths: 255 nm (band width 
16 nm); and 

e) Pump Pressure: 15 MPa. 


Clear observation can be made from the catechu dye 
sample as can be seen in the chromatographs given 
in Fig. 2. 

Identification of compounds by HPLC is a crucial part 
of any HPLC assay. In order to identify any compound 
by HPLC, a detector must first be selected. UV detector 
may be selected and set to optimal detection settings, a 
separation assay is developed. The parameters of this 
assay may be made to be such that a clean peak of the 
both the samples are observed from the chromatograph. 
The experimental conditions are as following: 


a) Column: C18; 
b) Flow rate: 1.0 ml/min; and 
c) Detection wavelengths: 255 nm. 


IS 17211 : 2019 


Due care is to be taken to identify peak so that a 
reasonable retention time and well separated from 
extraneous peaks at the detection levels. Clear 
observation can be made from the catechu dye 
sample as can be seen in the chromatographs given in 
Fig. 2. Natural catechu has main peak at 2.5 min and a 
characteristic peak at 4.5 min.

C-6 CONCLUSION 


Natural catechu shows clear differences in its

ANNEX D 


( Clauses 1, 5.2 and 5.3 ) 


IDENTIFICATION OF NATURAL CATECHU DYE BY 
UV-VISIBLE SPECTROSCOPIC METHOD 


D-1 PRINCIPLE 


When sample molecules are exposed to light having 
an energy that matches a possible electronic transition 
within the molecule, some of the light energy will 
be absorbed as the electron is promoted to a higher 
energy orbital. An optical spectrometer records the 
wavelengths at which absorption occurs, together 
with the degree of absorption at each wavelength. The 
resulting spectrum is presented as a graph of absorbance 
(A) versus wavelength. 


Many molecules absorb ultra-violet or visible light. 
The absorbance of a solution increases as attenuation of 
the beam increases. Absorbance is directly proportional 
to the path length, 5, and the concentration, c, of the 
absorbing species. Beer's law states that: 


A = €bc 


Where, € is a constant of proportionality, called 
absorbtivity. 


Different molecules absorb radiation of different 
wavelengths. An absorption spectrum will show a 
number of absorption bands corresponding to structural 
groups within the molecule. Thus, the absorption 
spectra (optical density) of a particular dye at a 
particular wavelength is maximum. 


D-2 APPARATUS 


D-2.1 Ultra Violet — Visible spectrophotometer 
machine. 


D-2.2 Quartz Sample Tube (Cuvette) — Having 
1.00 cm light path. 


D-2.3 Electronic Balance — Resolution at 0.001g 
D-2.4 Spatula 
D-2.5 Whatmann Filter Paper — Grade 42 


D-3 REAGENT 


D-3.1 Natural Catechu Dye 
D-3.2 Methanol 


D-3.3 Dichloromethane 
NOTE — All reagents shall be of analytical purity. 


D-4 PROCEDURE 


D-4.1 The catechu dye is weighed 0.1g) and dissolved 
in 1 000 ml dichloromethane and scanned through 
UV-visible spectrometer. For visible spectrum this 
solution is used and for UV spectrum the solution is 
further diluted 5 times. Identification of the dye by 
this method involves an empirical comparison of the 
details of the spectrum, that is, lamda maxima (optical 
density) of natural Catechu and synthetic brown dye 
and the characteristic peaks are matched as shown 
in Fig. 3. The ultraviolet (UV) region scanned is 
normally from 200 to 400 nm, and the visible portion is 
from 400 to 800 nm.

D-6 CONCLUSION 


Lamda maxima (optical density) of natural catechu is 
very specific. In the UV spectrum, although the peaks 
are at 250 nm but with different optical densities (OD). 
In the visible region peaks at 450 nm natural catechu 
dyes are the characteristic peaks mentioned as shown 
in the spectra in Fig. 3. 


ANNEX E 
( Clause 1, 5.2 and 5.3 ) 


EXTRACTION OF NATURAL CATECHU DYE FROM 
DYED SWATCHES 


E-1 PRINCIPLE 


The solvent (in soxhlet) extraction of dyed samples 
is necessary to release the dyes from the dyed fabric 
samples. 


E-2 PROCEDURE 


The solvent (in soxhlet) extraction of dyed samples 
is necessary to release the dyes from the dyed cotton 
samples. Cotton samples 50 g dyed from natural 


catechu dye is cut into small pieces and packed in a 
filter paper as a filter paper column. The packed filter 
paper column is put for soxhlet extraction for 6-8 h 
with methanol as solvent for extraction, temperature is 
set at 60?C, till all the colour is discharged. Remove the 
solvent in a vacuum rotatory evaporator to dryness. The 
sample is now ready for used in chromatographic and 
spectroscopic analysis as per the methods described 
above.
